title: He thought he was ready.
paragraphs: That’s the part we don’t like to admit.

You saw something wrong.
You felt something burning.
You knew—“This has to change.”
But no one talks about what happens when passion outruns obedience.

Moses looked both ways before he struck (Exodus 2:12).
Not for God.

He checked if people were watching…
but didn’t check if God had spoken.
And in one moment, zeal became sin.

This wasn’t random anger.
This was misdirected calling.
Acts 7:25 says Moses supposed his people would understand that God would deliver them through him…
Because God never told Moses to act that way.

You can be called by God…
and still move in a way that God never commanded.

We feel the burden…
and crown ourselves the solution.

We sense purpose…
and skip surrender.

We carry conviction…
but refuse correction.
And somewhere deep inside, there’s a voice whispering:
“You don’t need to wait. Just act.”
But that voice isn’t always God.
Sometimes it’s pride dressed like urgency.
Sometimes it’s insecurity trying to prove something.
Sometimes it’s hidden frustration that hasn’t learned how to kneel yet.
What are you forcing right now that God never told you to carry?
What are you trying to fix with your hands that only God can redeem with His power?
The same passion that reveals your calling can also expose your immaturity.
And that difference cost him 40 years.
But because God refused to use an unbroken vessel for a holy assignment.
Hebrews 11:24–25 shows Moses would later choose suffering with God’s people over the pleasures of Egypt.

But before that faith…
there was failure.

Before the staff…
there was a sword.

Before deliverance…
there was a dead body in the sand.
And maybe that’s your story too.

Hidden compromises.
Delayed obedience.
Silent pride.

You still pray.
You still show up.
But there are areas where you’ve already decided:
This is where it gets real.
Because self-reliance doesn’t just slow your calling.
Moses tried to save one man by killing another.
Jesus came to save all men by giving Himself.

One acted in human strength.
The other moved in divine surrender.
You and I—we’ve all done this.
We’ve all tried to fix what only Christ can redeem.
We’ve all buried things we hoped no one would find.
But Numbers 32:23 says, “Be sure your sin will find you out.”
The next day, when he tried to play peacemaker, the Hebrew men said:
“Who made you ruler and judge over us?” (Exodus 2:14)
“You’re not sent. You just stepped in.”
That hit deeper than the crime.
Calling without confirmation leads to confusion.
And maybe someone needs to hear this:

Just because you feel ready…
doesn’t mean God has released you.

Just because it burns…
doesn’t mean it’s time.

Just because you can…
doesn’t mean you should.
Are you submitted… or just passionate?
Because passion can make you loud.
But only surrender makes you usable.
And this is where grace breaks in.
He sent him to the wilderness.
Acts 7:30 says after forty years, God appeared to Moses in a burning bush.
Because God is not just concerned with what you do.
He’s concerned with who you become.
God would rather delay your assignment than allow your pride to destroy it.
Jesus stretched out His hands in mercy.
Romans 5:8 declares that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Not when we got it right.
“I’ll carry what you tried to control.”
That’s why your story isn’t over.
You may have acted too soon.
If you lay down the need to control…

Because it means the pressure is off…
and the invitation is open.
If this hit something deep in you…
This isn’t about content. It’s about consecration.
we’ll talk about what Moses learned in the wilderness that changed everything.
